Profile by Local Expansion

Source: R/profile_approx.R
profile_taylor.Rd

Selects a method of statmod_profile() that does not refit. The coefficients that are not held are developed as a polynomial in the held ones around the estimate, and the log-likelihood and the penalty are computed exactly at the coefficients that the polynomial gives.

Usage

ProfileTaylor(name = character(0), order = integer(0))

profile_taylor(order = 2)

Arguments

name

The short name of the method, a single string. The class constructor ProfileTaylor() takes it, and profile_taylor() sets it to "taylor".

order

The highest order of the derivatives of the objective used, an integer from 2 to 5.

Value

A ProfileTaylor object, inheriting from profile_method, with the properties name and order.

Details

With \(\theta\) the held coefficients and \(\eta\) the others, the refitted \(\hat\eta(\theta)\) solves \(\nabla_\eta F(\eta, \theta) = 0\) for the objective \(F\) of the fit. Along the segment from the estimate to a point of the grid, the derivatives of \(\hat\eta\) are obtained one order after another: the first is \(-H_{\eta\eta}^{-1} H_{\eta\theta}\,\delta\), and each following one is minus \(H_{\eta\eta}^{-1}\) times the derivative of that order, along the segment, of the gradient evaluated at the polynomial of the lower orders. That derivative is taken by one central stencil of numericals7 on the analytic gradient. The polynomial has degree order - 1, so that order is the highest order of the derivatives of the objective that the expansion uses. The Hessian is the observed information of the fit, with, for a model with nonlinear or smoothed break-point terms, the term of the block that moves with its coefficients. With the log-likelihood and the penalty computed exactly at the predicted coefficients, the penalized log-likelihood of every row is a lower bound of the profile. The column converged is NA.

Quantities that the outer criterion estimates (coordinates, and hyperparameters with hyper = "refit") are developed as in profile_continuation(), from the derivatives of the criterion in those quantities, and the coefficients that are neither held nor estimated by the criterion are then the penalized mode at the predicted values (one inner fit for each point). The lower bound does not hold in that case, because the exact method maximizes the criterion and not the penalized log-likelihood over those quantities. A hyperparameter in which is held at the values of its grid on the scale of its link, and the column outer_criterion is the profile.

The requirements on the model are those of profile_continuation().

See also

statmod_profile(), profile_grid(), profile_continuation().

Examples

profile_taylor()
#> <statmodels7::ProfileTaylor>
#>  @ name : chr "taylor"
#>  @ order: int 2
profile_taylor(order = 4)
#> <statmodels7::ProfileTaylor>
#>  @ name : chr "taylor"
#>  @ order: int 4
